Quarterly Budget Forecast – Q3 2025

Our Q3 forecast projects total operating expenses of $1.24M, a 4.2% increase over Q2, driven primarily by the new hires in engineering and a scheduled cloud infrastructure upgrade. Revenue is expected to reach $1.58M, yielding a net margin of 21.5%, slightly below our target of 23% due to higher-than-anticipated marketing spend.

Key variances to watch:
- Salaries & wages: $620K (up 6% from Q2 due to two mid-month starts)
- Cloud hosting: $95K (up 12% as we migrate to the new region)
- Marketing: $180K (up 8% from the conference sponsorship)
- Office & admin: $45K (flat)

We’ve built in a 5% contingency for unplanned cloud overages. The finance team will review actuals against this forecast at the end of each month. Any deviation greater than 10% in a category requires a written explanation from the department lead.

Note: The forecast assumes no major changes in headcount beyond the two open roles in sales. If those roles are filled earlier, we may need to adjust the salary line upward by approximately $15K per quarter.

Your October cloud bill is now available. Total charges: $12,847.33, a 9% increase from September. The breakdown by service is as follows:

| Service          | Cost       |
|------------------|------------|
| Compute (EC2)    | $6,230.11  |
| Storage (S3)     | $1,845.22  |
| Database (RDS)   | $3,102.45  |
| Data Transfer    | $892.10    |
| Support          | $777.45    |

Most of the increase comes from additional EC2 instances spun up for the load testing on Oct 12–15. Those instances were terminated on Oct 16, so we expect November to return to normal levels. The support plan remains at Business tier.

If you have questions about this bill, contact billing@nimbuscloud.example. For cost optimization tips, see our guide at https://nimbuscloud.example/docs/cost-tips.
Effective November 1, 2025, all salaried employees will see a 3% cost-of-living adjustment in their paychecks, as approved in the Q3 board meeting.

We’ve processed the payroll change for Jordan Lee (employee ID 4821) to reflect the new remote work stipend of $50 per month. This adjustment will appear starting with the November 15 pay run. Jordan’s department manager, Priya, confirmed the change via email on October 20. The stipend is taxable and will be included in gross wages. If you have questions, please reach out to the HR service desk at hr@acme.example. Note that our payroll chatbot can now answer common questions about stipends and deductions—just type your question in the portal.

The updated budget forecast spreadsheet is now live in the shared drive. I’ve added a scenario tab for a 10% revenue shortfall and a tab for the cloud cost overrun we discussed. Please review the assumptions in the ‘Inputs’ sheet—especially the headcount and marketing spend—and add comments by Friday. The finance bot will automatically consolidate comments into a summary report on Monday morning.

Our cloud bill for November came in at $11,200, which is under budget by about $800. The savings came from rightsizing the RDS instances and moving cold data to Glacier. I’ve attached the detailed cost explorer export. The automated cost monitor didn’t flag any anomalies this month, so we’re on track. Next month we expect a slight increase due to the holiday traffic, but it should stay within the forecast.

Reminder: The payroll change for the new 401(k) match percentage (4% instead of 3%) takes effect on January 1. Employees who want to adjust their contribution should log into the payroll portal by December 15. The HR chatbot can walk you through the steps if you’re unsure. No action is needed if you’re keeping your current contribution rate.

I asked the budgeting assistant to pull last quarter’s actuals and compare them to the forecast. It highlighted that our cloud spend was 15% over, mainly due to the unexpected test environment. The assistant suggested we set up budget alerts at 80% and 100% thresholds. We’ll implement those alerts this week and review the forecast again next month.

The payroll team uses an automated tool to reconcile timesheets before each pay run. This month, the tool flagged three entries with missing project codes. Those have been corrected and the pay run will proceed as scheduled. If you receive a notification about a missing code, please update it in the time tracking system within 24 hours to avoid delays.

Our Q4 budget forecast includes a 12% increase in cloud costs due to the new data pipeline. To offset this, we’re reducing the travel budget by $20K and postponing the office furniture upgrade. The finance director will present the revised forecast at the all-hands on Thursday. A summary will be posted on the intranet afterward.
